scenes.caption: Read a suspicious message twice before you act.
scenes.say: A message arrives. Your account is frozen. Twenty four hours. A link. And an instruction to move your money to a safe account. Everything in it is built to move you before you think.

scenes.caption: Paste the message. It never leaves the page.
scenes.say: Second Read takes the message you actually have. You paste it, and it never leaves the page. No account, no upload, no network call.

scenes.caption: It counts kinds of pressure, not badness.
scenes.say: It does not give a score. It counts how many different kinds of pressure appear at once. No known pattern, a few signals, several, or many. And a message with no marks is called no known pattern, never safe.

scenes.caption: The words are marked in place. Nothing is rewritten.
scenes.say: The words are marked in place, in the sentence you were about to act on. Nothing is rewritten, so you can see the machinery inside the message itself.

scenes.caption: Every mark gets a reason and a different action.
scenes.say: Each mark gets a reason, and a different action. Not install it, call the number on the bank's own website. The alternative is the part that changes what happens next.

scenes.caption: Addresses are read without being opened.
scenes.say: Links are read without being opened, because opening them is the risk. Plain http, a cheap domain ending, a hyphen, and a bank's name sitting on a domain that is not the bank's.

scenes.caption: A channel the message cannot touch. Then a card for the fridge.
scenes.say: Then it names the channel the message cannot touch, with the three sentences to say on the call. And a card for the fridge: never read out a code, never move money to a safe account, never install what a stranger sent.

scenes.caption: Korean and English, for the reader it was built around.
scenes.say: All of it in Korean as well, because the people these messages reach are not reading security blogs in English at nine at night.

scenes.caption: 94 assertions in a real browser. Zero network calls.
scenes.say: Ninety four assertions run in a real browser, from the page itself. The suite checks that every rule fires, that ordinary messages stay quiet, and that a clean address is never called safe.

scenes.caption: Second Read — free, local, open source.
scenes.say: Second Read. Free, local, open source, and it works offline. Read it twice before you act.
